title: Polynomial-time selector test
statement: For every choice of the parameters $N,d,c,A,a$, the function sending a bit string $q$ to the one-bit string containing the selector value is polynomial-time computable. The selector is true exactly when either the fourth and first blocks of $q$ agree and the fifth and third blocks agree, or the fourth and third blocks agree and the fifth and second blocks agree, where block $i$ is the length-$|b|$ segment of the second pair projection of the first pair projection of $q$ beginning at offset $i|b|$, and $b$ is the second pair projection of the first pair projection of $q$.
hypotheses_covered: The parameters $N,d,c,A,a$ are arbitrary as quantified
caveat: The block extraction function has no supplied informal description; the statement spells out its displayed construction.
